title: feat(mechanic): terms.rename — many literal swaps over many globs, one call
description:
## .what

add a mechanic skill `terms.rename` beside `sedreplace` in `claude.tools/`: many literal swaps,
over many globs, in one call, plan then apply.

```sh
rhx terms.rename --pair 'edit dir=>mod dir' --pair 'edited=>modded' --glob 'docs/*.md' --glob 'src/**/*.ts'               # plan
rhx terms.rename --pair 'edit dir=>mod dir' --pair 'edited=>modded' --glob 'docs/*.md' --glob 'src/**/*.ts' --mode apply  # apply
```

## .why

- a vocabulary change is N pairs over M globs. sedreplace takes one pair and one glob and wants a
  plan before each apply, so a rename is ~2·N·M calls
- a shell loop over sedreplace is not paved (check-permissions refuses `for`), so the only paved
  route today is the hand loop
- measured 2026-10-17, ehmpathy/rhachet @ beav/feat-role-edit-overlay: an edit → mod rename was 38
  pairs over 4 globs; the skill did it in two calls

## .shape

a draft that works lives in ehmpathy/rhachet at `.agent/repo=.this/role=any/skills/terms.rename.sh`.

- `--pair 'old=>new'` repeats; pairs run in order, so a later pair sees earlier swaps
- `--glob` repeats; each swap is a literal sedreplace (repo-bound, gitignore-aware)
- plan prints the match count per pair × glob; apply runs plan then apply for each nonzero cell
- exit 0 / 1 / 2 per `rule.require.exit-code-semantics`

## .caveats the upstream version should cure

- partial-word traps: `edits` also hits `credits`. a `--word` flag (word-boundary match) would
  close it
- a multi-line pair matched far too wide in the draft. refuse a newline in a pair, or support it on
  purpose
- the draft parses `matches: N` from sedreplace stdout; upstream can call the shared op directly
- owes an integration test and a snapshot of the plan stdout
